title: Playing without music, memorising, B-flat transposition
summary: He explains memorising tunes, relying on the piano player and cornet transposition.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yes, that's correct. They used to harmonise instead of singing together why you play your instrument together. But you've got to practice a lot to be able to find out where those notes were on those horns. But that's not the way really. You have to learn how to read if you're going to play. But we don't use music nowadays because it's better to play without it. Because you know it's better, you're not burdened with looking at a part to play concert or do anything. We don't use music. You memorise everything.

If you memorise the melody, well the piano player naturally has to memorise the harmony, the bass player, and the guitar player and all the others. Whereas the horns just have to memorise the melody and know their harmony, know their harmony so that they can, or even listen to the harmonies and have a good enough trained ear to be able to hear those harmonies, hear what those chords are.
And if you don't know what the chord is, I'll turn around to the piano player. What is that chord then?

What is that? He'll say D7. And I think, having played the violin, I think everything concert. We call it concert which is the way it is on the violin or the piano.. That's concert. Now on my horn I play a B Flat instrument. So my Concert C on the cornet I mean my C on a B Flat instrument which is a cornet, is a B Flat, on piano. So I'm one tone above concert. So if a piano player turns around and says this tune is in the key of B Flat concert that we're going to play you know. Let's play the blues in B Flat say, I know that....
Which is very popular for blues isn't it? A very popular key for blues, yes?

That's right. It's C on the cornet. It's C on the cornet, you see. Now if he says, the piano player says this, we'll play the blues in C, that's my D. One tone above. So I know the key. But I know that the harmonies, the changes progress a certain way usually unless they're a little different at times. And then if I don't hear it with my ear, which is a well trained ear, if I don't hear it, I'll ask the piano player afterwards, what was that chord there in the second bar, the third bar or the bridge what was the chord, that second change and he will tell me what it is. I always ask what is it concert? And

he tells me and then I'll know exactly what it is. Instead of, maybe he's playing a certain inversion that's complicated. An inversion or something like that I couldn't hear it too well. If I didn't hear the bass notes. But you must be able to read. I'm so happy about the musicians nowadays as compared to us musicians years and years ago. Fifty years ago. They're smart enough to study now and study well and learn all their harmonies and they study their instruments. And they're much better, much finer musicians really than we were when we started out.
